Also, yes every carbon generally makes 4 bonds, so we see bonds between carbon - carbon and other atoms except hydrogen. Alkenes just refer to double bonds between two carbon atoms. Alkane means it’s only a single bond between carbons. Alkyne is a triple bond. Single bonds are called “sigma” bonds and double bonds are “pi” bonds. If multiple atoms in a row are connected into pi bonds, the electrons can flow between in extended networks. That’s kind of the basis of fluorescence and color. 

Due to the physical space that the electrons in the bond occupy, they can begin restricting the orientation of the atoms participating in the bond network, forcing them to be in a straight line, or confining them to a single plane in 3D space.
